summary: Creates a registry for smime-type Content-Type parameter values, registers current values, and sets rules for new ones. This makes it easier to find and add values.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 7114 creates one IANA list for S/MIME smime-type parameter values that were defined across several RFCs. It records the existing values and explains the requirement for adding new ones.

subtitle: Creates an IANA registry for S/MIME smime-type parameter values.

tldr.problem: S/MIME smime-type values had been defined in several documents without a central registry.
tldr.mechanism: IANA creates a subregistry, records the existing values, and uses Specification Required for new registrations.
tldr.outcome: RFC 7114 establishes a common registry and documents the current parameter values.

today: RFC 7114 is a Proposed Standard. The unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: Why a Registry Was Needed
sections.content: S/MIME defines the smime-type parameter for the application/pkcs7-mime media type. New parameter values had been added by several documents, but RFC 5751 did not create a registry for them. RFC 7114 establishes a registry and registers the values already defined in published documents.
sections.plainLanguage: Different documents had added values for the same S/MIME parameter. This RFC creates a central list for those values.

sections.title: The smime-type Registry
sections.content: IANA created the Parameter Values for the smime-type Parameter subregistry under MIME Media Type Sub-Parameter Registries. The initial registry contains ten values, each with a reference to its defining document. Examples include certs-only, enveloped-data, and signed-data.
sections.plainLanguage: The registry starts with ten values and points to the document that defines each one. This makes the existing options easier to identify.

sections.title: Adding Future Values
sections.content: New values may be registered using the Specification Required policy defined in RFC 5226. The S/MIME Message Specification in RFC 5751 gives guidance for assigning new smime-type parameter values, and that guidance applies to this registry.
sections.plainLanguage: A new value needs a specification under the stated registration policy. RFC 5751's guidelines apply to assigning it.
